n: Still at the Last Supper, Jesus comforts his anxious disciples: don’t let your hearts be troubled. You trust God — trust me too.

f.w: Let not your heart be troubled

n: His Father’s house has many dwelling places, and he is going ahead to prepare one for them. Latter-day revelation teaches that heaven has many kingdoms and degrees of glory.

f.w: many mansions

n: Having prepared a place, he will come again and take them to himself, so they can be where he is. His goal is to be together with them forever.

f.w: I will come again

n: He tells them they already know the way to where he is going.

f.w: the way ye know
f.g: They know the way because they know him (verse 6).

n: Honest Thomas speaks up: they don’t even know where he’s going, so how could they know the way?

f.w: Thomas

n: Jesus answers with one of his most famous statements: he himself is the Way, the Truth, and the Life. No one reaches the Father except through him.

f.w: I am the way, the truth, and the life

n: Knowing Jesus means knowing the Father. From now on, he says, they do know the Father and have seen him — in the Son.

f.w: ye should have known my Father also

n: Philip asks Jesus simply to show them the Father — that would be enough for them.

f.w: it sufficeth us

n: Gently but with some sadness, Jesus asks whether Philip still doesn’t know him after all this time. Anyone who has seen Jesus has seen what the Father is like — his character, love, and will.

f.w: he that hath seen me hath seen the Father

n: The Father and the Son dwell in each other in perfect unity; Jesus’s words and works are the Father’s.

f.w: I am in the Father, and the Father in me

n: Believe his word about that unity — or if that’s hard, believe because of the works he does.

f.w: for the very works' sake

n: Those who believe in him will do the works he does — and even greater ones — because he is going to the Father and will send the Spirit. His disciples would spread the gospel across the world.

f.w: greater works than these shall he do

n: Whatever they ask in his name he will do, so that the Father is glorified through the Son. Praying “in his name” means asking in harmony with his will and character.

f.w: whatsoever ye shall ask in my name

n: Jesus repeats the promise for emphasis.

f.w: If ye shall ask any thing in my name

n: Love for Christ is shown by keeping his commandments — obedience is love in action.

f.w: If ye love me, keep my commandments

n: Jesus will ask the Father to send them “another Comforter” to be with them forever. While Jesus had been their comforter in person, the Holy Ghost will now take that role.

f.w: another Comforter
f.g: Greek paraklētos — one called alongside to help: advocate, counselor, encourager.

n: This Comforter is the Spirit of truth. The world can’t receive him because it neither sees nor knows him, but the disciples know him, for he is with them and will be in them.

f.w: the Spirit of truth

n: He will not leave them as orphans; he will come to them — after his resurrection, through the Spirit, and in personal visitations.

f.w: comfortless
I will come to you

n: Soon the world will no longer see him, but they will. Because he lives, they too will live — his resurrection guarantees theirs.

f.w: because I live, ye shall live also

n: In that day they will understand the deep unity between the Father and the Son, and between Christ and his disciples.

f.w: ye in me, and I in you

n: Whoever keeps his commandments truly loves him, will be loved by the Father, and Jesus will love him and reveal himself to him.

f.w: will manifest myself to him

n: Another Judas — not Iscariot, probably the apostle also called Thaddeus — asks why Jesus will reveal himself to them but not to the whole world.

f.w: Judas saith unto him, not Iscariot

n: Jesus answers that the Father and the Son will come and make their home with anyone who loves him and keeps his word. Latter-day revelation teaches that this describes a personal appearance of the Father and the Son.

f.w: we will come unto him, and make our abode with him

n: Those who don’t love him don’t keep his words — and those words come from the Father.

f.w: is not mine, but the Father's which sent me

n: He has told them these things while still with them in person.

f.w: being yet present with you
f.g: A hint that his physical presence is about to end.

n: After he leaves, the Holy Ghost, sent by the Father in Jesus’s name, will teach them everything and bring back to their memory all Jesus said. This promise underlies the Gospel writers’ inspired recollection.

f.w: the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost
bring all things to your remembrance

n: His parting gift is peace — his own peace, not the shallow, temporary peace the world offers. So they need not be troubled or afraid.

f.w: my peace I give unto you

n: If they truly loved him, they would be glad he is returning to the Father, for the Father is greater than he is. The Father and the Son are distinct, and the Son honors the Father as his superior.

f.w: my Father is greater than I

n: He tells them in advance so that when these events happen, their faith will hold.

f.w: that, when it is come to pass, ye might believe

n: He won’t talk much longer, for the “prince of this world” — Satan — is coming. But Satan has no hold or claim on Jesus at all.

f.w: the prince of this world
hath nothing in me
f.g: Satan has no foothold — no sin or weakness in Jesus to grab onto.

n: Jesus goes to the cross to show the world his love for the Father and his perfect obedience. Then he says, “Get up, let’s go” — perhaps leaving the upper room, with chapters 15–17 spoken on the way.

f.w: as the Father gave me commandment, even so I do
Arise, let us go hence
